since the algo decided to show this to 400k+ people & I’ve gotten loads of dms saying it resonated, I decided to write a little guide on how to love & occasionally weaponize your flaws.

moving to SF in feb changed a lot for me, but I think this holds regardless:

1. expose yourself to new training data - you’re never gonna get anywhere solely by reasoning about your flaws in a vacuum. often what you’re convinced people don’t like about you is actually far from the worst thing about you in others’ eyes. sometimes what repels you about yourself might even be magnetic to certain others!

2. desensitize yourself to harsh truths - I may love some of my flaws, but I am still hyper aware of them and know I need to, for instance, dial back the texting or information overload in new friendships / relationships. I think about a lot of things, internal and external, and sometimes use texts like stream of consciousness journals. some people love this. other people find it tedious or overwhelming or think I’m manic - but I’m just like this! that doesn’t mean I need to lobotomize myself, but maybe just learn pacing.

3. put yourself in new environments - often it’s not that there’s something wrong with you, but that you’re poorly calibrated to the environment you’re in. you can absolutely learn to assimilate by hillclimbing ConformityBench, but there are diminishing returns to becoming more palatable to people whose approval would require sanding off everything interesting about you. better to find the environments that best foster the kind of growth you want.

4. distinguish between flaws, features, and uncalibrated intensity - some traits are genuinely maladaptive, while others are virtues with bad timing, and others just need the volume / intensity dialed down a bit. intensity is actually a feature if you consider your experience of life might actually outweigh the net detriment of your intensity. verbosity can be annoying, but it can also attract almost 18.5k followers on twitter. sensitivity requires building thick skin, sure, but it’s also signal detection. sometimes the goal is to calibrate your trait intensity to your environment, not to delete the trait.

5. let your flaws do some filtering - not everyone disliking you is a tragedy lol. there ARE people whose opinions should not matter to you. the people who are repelled by your baseline personality are often doing you the favor of removing themselves from your search space. let them churn.

conclusion:

the point isn’t to become universally likable. that would be model collapse.

the point is to be honest enough to see which parts of you need work, confident enough not to amputate the parts that make you vivid, and socially calibrated enough to know the difference.

glhf

$MU $SNDK $DRAM BOOM 

The auto industry faces a severe, underreported DRAM shortage that could disrupt vehicle production far more structurally than the 2021 chip crisis.

The core problem is a collision of three forces. Modern vehicles now require up to 150 microprocessors each, making DRAM as essential as steel. At the same time, AI and data center demand now consumes roughly 70% of global memory production by end of 2026. 

Hyperscalers pay 3 to 5x higher margins than automakers, so Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are reallocating capacity toward HBM. Automotive gets whatever is left.

The third force is the most dangerous. DDR4 and LPDDR4, the memory standard used in over 80% of vehicles today, is being discontinued. Prices are already up 70 to 100%. By 2028 these parts will simply not exist at any price.

Most major automakers including Ford, GM, Stellantis, VW, Hyundai, and Rivian are locked into Qualcomm's SA8295P chip which only supports LPDDR4. Migrating to LPDDR5 requires new SoC design, PCB redesign, and full ISO 26262 safety recertification, a process that takes 12 to 24 months minimum.

Friday's action did some serious degradation of the daily chart for $LPTH - short of an Emil handout of taxpayer monies I would not expect any momentum near term in the PPS. 

Without a good chart all we have is a thesis, which is where I expect us to be for a while.    

A short(er) term catalyst is now off the table and kicked to apparently spring 2027, one that it appears quite a few people were positioned for based on the loss of 1/5th of the market cap Fri.  Many of those who left will not be returning soon.  

After a massive 2025, 2026 has been a consolidation period and chopfest on the daily.  +850% gains take time to digest.  A failed breakout in May 26 simply said the stock is not ready and needed more time. 

Full year fiscal earnings will be reported in September but based on the past that has rarely been a catalyst for PPS movement; the stock has in fact gone down or flat next day, even when besting analyst estimates by huge margins and displaying 100% YoY growth.  It would appear much of that future growth was baked in, in the 2025 and very early 2026 PPS growth.

The stock fell to the 200 week moving average which has never been punctured aside July 2026, since it broke above it in April 2025.   The stock can still be "ok" even if it breaks it again (but it wouldn't be the best outcome), as long as it holds the bottom of this blue box which is ~$9.

A break below $9 would bring a different dimension of issues.  

The stock does remain in a 24 year base breakout vs $7.87.  I'd be shocked to see that break.

They weren't going to make it that easy; it almost never is.   Welcome to being a "community member".

> [@fundmyfund](https://twitter.com/fundmyfund):
> After having some time to digest the NGSRI news
> 
> • Sam was oozing confidence about the $LPTH / $LMT product as recently as a widely disseminated video interview 2 weeks ago.
> 
> • If a vendor can come and knock out in <8 months (Sep 26-May 27) what $RTX and $LMT have been working on for 3 years hats off to them.  But even THEN the DOW wants multiple vendors in their programs to get away from the last X decades of relying on sole vendors. 
> 
> • Any technology solution in the next <8 months surely won't be an "off the shelf" solution.
> 
> • A theory exists that $RTX is doing so poorly, the DOW wants another vendor competing with $LMT "down the line" as $RTX gets pushed out.  That would be an uber bullish viewing but I try not to drink the Kool Aid.  But I would be tickled if this is the outcome.
> 
> • While we like to think $LPTH as our little undiscovered baby, there have been some big accounts who have glommed onto the story in the past 1-4 months which have brought a lot of attention to the name.  In retrospect more than I realized.  These accounts bring "hot money" but often not "lasting money" - many of their followers want near instant results or they are gone.  Fair play - that comes with more attention.  The price reaction function yesterday makes clear to me that this isn't the little quiet name very few know about, as it was in Sept 2025 when some of us first got into the story. 
> 
> • The only thing that would change my thesis about NGSRI specific is the Army pushing out the date when they want vendors to start delivering product, which at this point remains fiscal 2028.  That begins Oct 1, 2027 and ends Sep 30, 2028.   Buying 11,000 missiles in that time frame means a company needs to be in FRIP (full rate production) by winter 27-28 at the latest - preferably earlier.  Reverse engineering means LRIP (low rate production) by next summer at the latest - preferably earlier but after this announcement it won't be earlier.  Hence if we see a notice the ENTIRE program has been pushed out a year to Fiscal Year 2029 that would be the time to ask serious questions. We are not there.
> 
> • Some have said this action was well known to management in advance - if so my only qualm in this situation is that this sort of information should have been publicly messaged to the market because it obviously caught the masses by surprise.  The market takes "bad news" better than "uncertainty".  Maybe a small lesson for a management which until 6 months ago had almost zero attention on it.  And now has many more eyes on it.  Expectation setting matters.
> 
> • This management is more about putting their head down & growing the business and not as much about optics (pun intended).  They don't provide guidance, they now are only announcing large contracts and shunning press releases of any smaller orders, have a less frequent interview cadence then similar sized companies, etc.  I don't see those things changing however I do think it was a misstep to at some point in the last 6 months not tell the investor base "understand it is typical for the Army to open up the competition one last time in the closing moments" (or however it needs to be said more accurately).  For example Allan at $UMAC has told us in advance the company will need to change auditors as it nears a $100M annual revenue run rate because SOX compliance comes into frame and their current auditor doesn't offer that.  An auditor change often leads to panic in the retail investor base and PPS reduction because people think the current auditor found something unbecoming and management is getting rid of the dirty laundry.  So this has been telegraphed in advance at $UMAC ; hence this event at $LPTH  - if known by management in advance - would have been nice to have been telegraphed in advance.
> 
> • I am segregating the 2 new items - (a) new competitors invited ("pretty standard these days") and (b) timeline pushed out from fall 2026 to spring 2027.  Management most likely was not aware of the latter so no communication expected on that front; but communication on the former would have been helpful.
> 
> • Everything else remains intact including executive orders, anti Chinese supply chain movement, germanium price increases, Chinese hoarding of germanium, and design plans (often for 10+ year programs) that seek non germanium solutions.  Some have offered there are non $LPTH solutions for this suite of issues and opportunities which is fine - of course there is competition and everyone can have their opinion on ultimate winners.  Pros for $LPTH are - it's domestic, it has the exclusive Navy lab patent, it has the largest suite of non germanium solutions (now up to 20 with the acquisition of Amorphous Materials), it's in the public sphere, it has a war chest that a public company offers that is more difficult for a private company to generate, it has a suite of potential government cash infusion opportunities, etc.  But that's what makes a market - you can bet your thesis 5 days a week, 52 weeks a year.
> 
> • Since following the story approximately 1 year ago, I have yet to see management failing to deliver on what has been outlined product wise.  The only 'faults' have been things out of their control namely timing issues such as the border surveillance program.  Which now after being a private enterprise investor for years until pivoting to a slew of companies in the defense sector recently, I have learned is part of the devil's bargain. SECTOR ROTATION UPDATE:

I’m comparing the last 8 days vs. the 5-month trend because short-term rotation can tell us where momentum is shifting before the longer-term picture catches up.

And this week, there are some BIG changes 👀

SHORT-TERM LEADERS:

XLE XLK XLB XLV

Energy remains the standout, continuing to show strong relative strength. I suspect energy names to be in the leader or weakening quadrants depending on any war news that comes out. 

XLV is the big mover here, it went from Weakening → Leading since last week thanks to MRNA news. 

XLB remains strong as well, while XLK is showing a very interesting short-term divergence from its longer-term position.

IMPROVING

XLC

Communication Services remains in the Improving quadrant.

Not leading yet, but the rotation is moving in the right direction. This is the type of sector I’d keep on the radar for confirmation.

WEAKENING

XLY

Consumer Discretionary improved from Lagging → Weakening over the past week.

That’s an improvement, but it hasn’t yet reached the point where I’d consider the sector a leader.

LAGGING

XLK XLU XLI

The biggest short-term deterioration is XLK.

Last week, XLK was sitting in Leading.

Now it has rotated into Lagging.

That’s a significant shift in relative momentum and something I’ll be watching closely.

NOW LOOK AT THE 5-MONTH VIEW

The longer-term picture looks very different:

Leading: XLF XLE
Improving: XLB XLV XLC
Weakening: XLK
Lagging: XLU XLI XLY

This is why I don’t like looking at RRG in isolation.

The short-term chart tells you where rotation is happening NOW.

The 5-month chart tells you whether that rotation is happening within a broader trend.

For example:

XLK:
5-month = Weakening
8-day = Lagging

That suggests the recent deterioration is becoming more significant.

XLV:
5-month = Improving
8-day = Leading

That’s a much more constructive transition, longer-term improvement is now showing up in the short term.

XLB:
5-month = Improving
8-day = Leading

Another sector where short-term momentum is confirming the longer-term improvement.

XLF:
5-month = Leading
8-day = Leading

That’s one of the cleaner setups on the board.. strength on both timeframes.

XLE:
Leading on both.

Energy continues to stand out as one of the strongest areas of the market.

The biggest lesson: don’t just ask “Which sector is strongest?”

Instead, ask:

Where is relative strength improving?
Where is it deteriorating?
And is the short-term rotation confirming or contradicting the longer-term trend?

That’s where RRG becomes much more useful.

I’ll be watching these rotations closely heading into next week. 👀

Pyth launched its Data Marketplace in April 2026. Fidelity Euronext Tradeweb and major market makers signed on. The platform lets institutions publish proprietary data (ETF fair value pricing FX rates precious metals data) on chain while keeping control and monetization of that data.

Euronext brought institutional spot FX NDF and precious metals pricing into Pyth Pros feeds.

=> Pyth Pro: actual revenue

Pyth Pro is a paid subscription for institutions wanting premium, low-latency data feeds. It crossed $1M in annual recurring revenue shortly after launch. Most crypto products generate zero revenue. This one has paying enterprise customers including Kalshi the first CFTC regulated prediction market in the US which adopted Pyth Pro to help resolve commodities and real world asset markets.

=> The government angle

The US Department of Commerce selected Pyth to help publish official economic data, including GDP figures, on-chain. $PYTH spiked over 70% in 24 hours when the news broke.

A government body validated the project directly. It opens the door to more datasets, employment numbers and inflation data among them, and positions Pyth as core infrastructure for the broader push to put public data on chain.

=> The PYTH Reserve

In December 2025 Pyth introduced the PYTH Reserve a mechanism that takes a share of protocol revenue from Pyth Pro and the Data Marketplace and uses it for systematic monthly buybacks of PYTH tokens. As the business earns some of that money buys $PYTH off the market.

Few oracle tokens attempt a direct revenue to token link like this. Most rely on speculation or staking emissions.

=> Scale

Pyth supports over 100 blockchains and runs 3000+ live price feeds as of late 2025, with targets of 10000+ by end of 2026 and 50000+ by 2027. Its share of the decentralized oracle sector grew to roughly 13% closing the gap on Chainlink.

Pyth started with a handful of crypto price feeds on Solana. It now touches equities FX commodities and macro data across chains.

=> Tokenomics and unlocks

Pyth has a 10B max supply and roughly 21% of total supply remains locked scheduled to unlock around May 2027. The previous unlock 2.13B tokens in May 2025/2026 preceded a 22%+ correction and that was a smaller event.

New supply hitting the market faster than demand absorbs it creates downward pressure. This is the biggest near term headwind for $PYTH.

=> Bull case

Pyth Reserve buybacks scale as Pyth Pro and Data Marketplace revenue grows. More government and institutional partnerships land. Oracle market share keeps climbing against Chainlink. A broader crypto bull cycle lifts mid caps.

=> Bear case

Token unlocks outpace organic buy pressure. Institutional adoption doesnt translate into token demand if TradFi clients pay in stablecoins or fiat instead of PYTH. Chainlink and other oracles compete harder. Altcoin weakness drags down fundamentally improving projects anyway.

=> Where the price could go

Analyst models for 2026 split widely. Some see PYTH stuck in the $0.03 $0.08 range under unlock pressure. More optimistic takes tied to institutional traction put a 2026 target around $0.30 to $0.35.

Long range models for 2030 suggest $2 to $2.50+ if Pyth becomes a real TradFi data standard and the Reserve buyback scales.

The gap between those numbers comes down to one question: does institutional revenue grow faster than token supply unlocks ?

=> My take

$PYTH is one of the more interesting infrastructure plays in crypto. It isnt a meme or a narrative pump. Its a project competing with Bloomberg and Refinitiv style data businesses with real institutional and government attention behind it.

Tokenomics drag on it and two years of price action reflect that. Watch the fundamentals and let the buyback mechanism prove itself over multiple quarters.

=> TLDR

Real product real institutional clients: Fidelity Euronext Tradeweb, Kalshi. A US government partnership through the Dept. of Commerce. A new buyback mechanism in the PYTH Reserve. Heavy token unlocks through 2027. Price still down 96% from ATH.

The next 12 to 18 months answer the question: does $PYTH become financial infrastructure, or stay another oracle token waiting on hype?

Sleeping giant or slow bleed? Drop your 2026 price target.
